title: The first shall be last (Matthew 19:16–30)
hook: every box ticked, and still: what lack I yet?
tomorrow: a mother asks for the best seats for her sons. what does he say?

segments.voice: That was a week down a mountain: arise, be not afraid; faith the size of a seed; angels before God's face; two or three; seventy times seven; and children blessed. Yesterday's line: of such is the kingdom.
screen: `OF SUCH IS THE KINGDOM.` → `A WEEK DOWN THE MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: Every box ticked: the grades, the volunteer hours, the résumé line. And still a quiet question underneath. A young man brings exactly that to Jesus: "Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?" Keep the commandments, Jesus says, and names them. All these I have kept, the young man answers. Then the question that answers yesterday's teaser: "what lack I yet?"
screen: `EVERY BOX TICKED.` → `WHAT GOOD THING SHALL I DO?` → `WHAT LACK I YET?`

segments.voice: Jesus answers him: "If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me." And Matthew tells us what happens next. "But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions." Not angry. Sorrowful. Then the camel and the needle, and the disciples, amazed: "Who then can be saved?" Jesus: "With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible." And Peter, being Peter, asks what about us; we left everything. Jesus promises them much, and then folds a warning into the promise: "But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first." The young man walked away holding what he had. Peter stayed and started counting what he'd given. The same reversal answers both: the order you expect isn't the kingdom's order. Christians read sell that thou hast in more than one way: some as a call for a few, some as a test of whatever each person holds tightest.
screen: `SELL, GIVE, COME, FOLLOW.` · `HE WENT AWAY SORROWFUL.` · `WITH GOD ALL THINGS ARE POSSIBLE.` · `PETER: WHAT ABOUT US?` · then, large: `FIRST WILL BE LAST.`

segments.voice: Pick one privilege you could hand to someone else this week: the front seat, the first pick, the last word. Name it, then name what makes letting go of it hard. Then choose the moment you'll hand it over, and hold that plan quietly while you breathe.
The first shall be last. The kingdom's reversal, told to a rich young man who left and to Peter who stayed.
screen: `THE FIRST SHALL BE LAST — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: first will be last. The young man had kept every rule and still walked away. A week, done.

howItsDone: Some Christians, in religious orders and elsewhere, have taken 'sell that thou hast' as a call to give up possessions; others read it as asking each person to let go of whatever they hold tightest.

fork.setup: a friend has done every item on her church's volunteer list and asks, honestly: what am I still missing? what did Jesus' answer to the rich young man point at?
